findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a concrete per-test proving step for the Windows AC: confirm the sweep emits per-test outcomes (e.g. -rA or junit), then check that all 27 removed node ids appear as PASSED (count == 27) and none as SKIPPED.
evidence: "find the run ... and get the `sweep (windows)` job id from `gh run view <run> --json jobs`" — the steps end here
AC: "Every line removed ... names a test that ran and passed (not skipped)"
VERIFY taxonomy (5): no cardinality assertion when the criterion names a count (27)
findings.finding: The Windows verification steps stop at obtaining the sweep job id. They never say how to prove, per node id, that each of the 27 tests 'ran and passed (not skipped)'. A default or -q pytest log does not list passed tests by name, so the AC's instrument (`gh run view --job <id> --log`) may not show per-test outcomes. The plan also has no count assertion that all 27 appear as PASSED.
scenarios: The sweep job concludes success, but some of the 27 were skipped on Windows (e.g. a platform skipif in the repo-isolation guard). Without per-test PASSED lines this goes unnoticed and the AC is attested falsely.
findings.suggested_fix: Save the removed node ids to a list before deleting the file. After the run, execute `gh run view --job <id> --log | grep -F -f removed_ids.txt | grep -c ' PASSED'` and require 27, plus a zero-match check for SKIPPED. If the sweep runs pytest without -rA or -v, state that the run's junit artifact is used instead.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the Windows branch's `== _child_env(caller_env)` oracle with an independent expectation: the caller's keys plus only `SYSTEMROOT` from the ambient environment, with no other ambient key present.
evidence: "assert captured["env"] == _child_env(caller_env) otherwise"
Plan: GitHub is a read-only mirror, so there is no pre-merge Windows run.
findings.finding: On Windows, the updated call-contract test asserts `captured["env"] == _child_env(caller_env)`, which compares the helper's output with the same helper's output. It is tautological. If `_child_env` added the wrong key, forwarded an ambient secret, or returned the caller's object unchanged, this assertion would still pass. On POSIX the branch never runs, so the Windows plumbing is never checked against an independent oracle.
scenarios: A future regression makes `_child_env` forward the whole ambient environment on nt. The Windows call-contract test still passes because both sides of the comparison call the same broken function.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert this in the Windows branch: `captured["env"]` has exactly the keys of `caller_env` plus `SYSTEMROOT` when the caller had no case-insensitive SYSTEMROOT key, `captured["env"]["SYSTEMROOT"] == os.environ["SYSTEMROOT"]`, and every caller value is unchanged.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In Approach step 1, say that `_child_env` builds its copy with the mapping's own `.copy()` (which `SubprocessEnv.copy()` keeps as a `SubprocessEnv`) and then sets `SYSTEMROOT`, instead of a bespoke type-preserving constructor.
evidence: Plan: "The copy keeps the caller's mapping type (`SubprocessEnv` stays `SubprocessEnv`, so its redacted repr survives)"
tests/_subprocess_env.py:22-24 `def copy(self) -> Self: """Copy without dropping the representation-safety boundary.""" return type(self)(self)`
tests/_subprocess_env.py:26-32 `with_overrides` returns `self.copy()` updated with overrides
Callers pass plain dicts (test_environ_assert_repr_security.py:136) or SubprocessEnv (test_nested_pytest_helper.py:27 `env=subprocess_env()`), both of which have a type-correct `.copy()`
findings.finding: The plan requires that `_child_env`'s copy 'keeps the caller's mapping type (`SubprocessEnv` stays `SubprocessEnv`...)' but does not say how. The codebase already solves type-preserving copies: `SubprocessEnv.copy()` returns `type(self)(self)` and `with_overrides(...)` returns a boundary-preserving updated copy. If the helper uses its own construction (e.g. `type(env)({**env, ...})`) instead, it duplicates that boundary logic, and the two can drift if SubprocessEnv's copy semantics change.
scenarios: A future change to SubprocessEnv's copy/redaction boundary is not picked up by a hand-rolled copy in `_child_env`, and the redacted repr is silently lost in the Windows path.
findings.suggested_fix: In `_child_env`, for the add case: `child = env.copy() if hasattr(env, "copy") else dict(env); child["SYSTEMROOT"] = ambient_value; return child`. This reuses `SubprocessEnv.copy()` (tests/_subprocess_env.py:22) so the redaction boundary has a single definition.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Rebuild the run_nested_pytest consumer census with find_referencing_symbols on run_nested_pytest, plus a string grep for env assertions in its callers (`["env"] is`, `["env"] ==`, `kwargs["env"]`, os.environ-content probes, monkeypatched subprocess.run), and record the result in place of the single-grep census sentence.
evidence: Plan text: "A census of `tests/` for assertions on a captured `env` (`grep -rn '\["env"\] is'`) finds no other identity check on this helper's output.": the plan itself says the inventory came from a grep.

run_nested_pytest has about 40 call sites, including tests/_store_isolation.py:33, tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_env_repr_security.py:24, tests/unit/test_crash_guard.py (5 sites), tests/unit/test_timeout_budget.py (5 sites) and tests/unit/test_engine_dir.py:184/239. None was checked through a reference lookup.

tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_deadline.py:47/78 monkeypatch guard_test.subprocess.run under the reach of run_nested_pytest, so they capture kwargs from the helper. The pattern `["env"] is` would not have surfaced them for review.
findings.finding: run_nested_pytest's env pass-through contract changes on Windows, and the plan's inventory of affected callers and assertions came from one hand grep ('grep -rn '\["env"\] is''), not from a symbol-reference lookup. That pattern only catches identity checks spelled exactly `["env"] is`. It misses exact-equality checks (`captured["env"] == {...}`), env captured under another name, and child probes that assert the exact contents of os.environ. All of these would break once SYSTEMROOT is added on Windows. My own sweep (about 40 call sites across about 25 files, plus the monkeypatched subprocess.run in test_repo_isolation_deadline.py) found no omitted site. Even so, the method is unsound and the result is unconfirmed.
findings.location: Approach step 2: "A census of `tests/` for assertions on a captured `env` (`grep -rn '\["env"\] is'`) finds no other identity check on this helper's output."
scenarios: A caller of run_nested_pytest asserts `captured["env"] == {...}`, or a child probe asserts exact os.environ contents. The `["env"] is` grep does not match it, so the caller is not updated and starts failing on the Windows sweep once _child_env adds SYSTEMROOT.

A future reader treats the grep census as a complete consumer list for the new Windows exception and does not re-check callers that capture env under another name (for example `seen_env`, or `kwargs` in test_repo_isolation_deadline.py).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the census sentence in Approach step 2 with: run_nested_pytest's references (from find_referencing_symbols, plus a string grep for 'run_nested_pytest' and for monkeypatched 'subprocess.run' in its callers) were checked for identity, equality or exact-content assertions on env. The only one is tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_helper.py:94.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add POSIX-runnable cases for the `_root_conftest` name match: a Windows-style backslash path matches via `PureWindowsPath`, a forward-slash POSIX path matches, and `xtests/conftest.py` is rejected.
evidence: "`Path(name).parts[-2:] == ("tests", "conftest.py")`"
"On POSIX it accepts exactly the names the old suffix accepted, except a sibling named `xtests/conftest.py`"
Testing lists new cases only for `_child_env`; none for `_root_conftest`.
findings.finding: The `_root_conftest` matching changes in two ways: it now accepts backslash-separated names, and it now rejects `xtests/conftest.py`. The Testing section adds no unit case for either. On POSIX, `Path` does not split backslash names, so the existing 8 tests only confirm the forward-slash case still works. The backslash case, which is the actual fix, is first exercised in the post-merge Windows sweep. The plan acknowledges that no pre-merge Windows run exists.
scenarios: The component-match expression is wrong for Windows names (for example, drive-anchored parts or case differences). `make verify` stays green, and the error surfaces only after merge, invoking the restore-the-deselect fallback.
findings.suggested_fix: Factor the name test into a small predicate that takes a path class, defaulting to `Path`. Parametrize it with `PureWindowsPath(r"D:\a\rebar\rebar\tests\conftest.py")` and `PurePosixPath("/x/tests/conftest.py")`, both expected to match, and `PurePosixPath("/x/xtests/conftest.py")`, expected to be rejected.
